items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with fp8 routed experts scores 10pp lower on AIME25 than vLLM (same weights, same node, same harness)
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] **The bug persists in the latest version.** — See "Version note" below. This was measured on **v0.5.17**, not the latest v0.5.19. v0.5.19 requires `torch==2.13.0` while this deployment is pinned to `torch 2.11.0+cu130` to stay aligned with the training stack; I did not want to report numbers from an unsupported torch/sglang combination. Happy to re-run on v0.5.19 if you can confirm the expected torch/flashinfer pairing.
- [x] Environment info and reproduction details are included below.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] Written in English.

### Describe the bug

On the **same machine, same weights, same harness, same sampling parameters, same day**, SGLang scores **10.2 points lower than vLLM on AIME25** for a DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint whose routed experts are **fp8**.

The official base model (fp4 routed experts) does **not** show this gap — it scores 95.83% under SGLang, in line with the ~96 reported in the SGLang cookbook. The gap appears only with the fp8-expert variant.

Runs were strictly sequential: SGLang was stopped and GPU memory fully released before vLLM was started, so the two never shared the GPUs.

#### Results — `sgl-eval run aime25`, 30 problems × 16 repeats = 480 samples

| | **SGLang 0.5.17** | **vLLM 0.28.0** |
|---|---|---|
| **pass@1[avg-of-16]** | **84.58%** ± 6.87 (SEM 1.72) | **94.79%** ± 4.21 (SEM 1.05) |
| majority@16 | 96.67% | 100.00% |
| pass@16 | 100.00% | 100.00% |
| **no_answer** | **4.17%** | **0.83%** |
| truncated_rate | 0.00% | 0.00% |
| error_rate | 0.00% | 0.00% |

The 10.2pp gap is far outside the SEM of either run.

#### The gap is mostly wrong answers, not lost answers

A natural first guess is that the parser is eating answers. Recomputing from the dumped predictions after excluding every `no_answer` case:

| | correct / answered | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| SGLang | 406 / 459 | **88.45%** |
| vLLM | 455 / 476 | **95.59%** |

Still a **7.1pp** gap. So `no_answer` accounts for only about a third of the difference — the majority is the model producing *wrong* answers under SGLang. That points at the generation path rather than the parsing layer.

`truncated_rate` is 0.00% on both sides, so this is not a `max_tokens` artifact.

### The distinguishing factor: fp8 routed experts

This is the same model family and the same SGLang version that works fine on the official base weights. The only difference is the expert quantization:

| | This checkpoint (gap) | Official base (no gap) |
|---|---|---|
| `expert_dtype` | **`"fp8"`** | `"fp4"` |
| `quantization_config.scale_fmt` | **`"float"`** (F32 block scale) | `"ue8m0"` |
| `quant_method` | `fp8` | `fp8` |
| `weight_block_size` | `[128, 128]` | `[128, 128]` |

Tensor names and shapes are identical between the two; they differ only in expert dtype and scale dtype (verified by a header-by-header comparison).

SGLang detects this correctly at startup:

```
Auto-detected DSV4 routed-expert layout: is_fp4_experts=False
```

and routes to `Fp8MoEMethod` + DeepGEMM, which is the expected path. Loading succeeds, there are no warnings, and throughput is normal — the output is simply less accurate.

**The weights are from an internal fine-tune and cannot be shared**, but they were produced by `ms-swift`'s `megatron export` with `fp8_recipe=blockwise` + `fp8_param_gather`, which yields exactly the `expert_dtype=fp8` / `scale_fmt=float` combination above. Any DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint exported that way should reproduce this. If it would help, I can run additional diagnostics on this checkpoint on request (e.g. greedy decoding traces, per-layer activation dumps).

### Reproduction

Both servers were started on the same 8×H200 node, one at a time.

**SGLang** (no `--moe-runner-backend marlin` — marlin MoE only engages when `is_fp4_experts` is true; passing it with fp8 experts fails with `no attribute 'runner'`):

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 \
  --tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --watchdog-timeout 1800 --enable-metrics
```

**vLLM** (official recipe, no extra env vars):

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"","reasoning_end_str":""}' \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001
```

**Evaluation** — identical against both endpoints:

```bash
sgl-eval run aime25 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1 \
  --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT --api-key EMPTY \
  --n-repeats 16 --max-tokens 200000 \
  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --thinking \
  --out-dir ./aime_out
```

### What I ruled out

Listing these so nobody re-treads the same ground:

1. **Chat template injecting tool scaffolding.** The model directory ships no `chat_template`, so each engine uses its own built-in. Measured `usage.prompt_tokens` on SGLang for a single-message request: **5 tokens** without `tools` vs **276** with one tool defined (the message itself is 1 token). So the no-tools template overhead is ~4 tokens — there is no hidden tool scaffolding in the prompt.
2. **`--moe-runner-backend marlin`.** Not applicable to fp8 experts (see above); auto-detection is doing the right thing.
3. **Truncation.** `truncated_rate` is 0.00% on both engines at `--max-tokens 200000`.
4. **`num_reasoning_tokens` reporting.** In the dumped predictions this is 0 for 100% of SGLang samples vs 0.21% for vLLM, which looks alarming but is unrelated: `sgl-eval` reads `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` (`sampler.py:172`), which SGLang does not populate. The reasoning content itself is still returned in `message.reasoning_content`.

### Environment

`python3 -m sglang.check_env` (version section; full NVIDIA topology omitted for length — 8×H200, NV18 all-to-all, 2 NUMA nodes):

```
Python: 3.12.13 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Jul  9 2026, 14:38:16) [GCC 14.3.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H200
GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86
CUDA Driver Version: 590.48.01
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
sglang: 0.5.17
sglang-kernel: 0.4.5
flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1
flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found
flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found
triton: 3.6.0
transformers: 5.12.1
torchao: 0.17.0
numpy: 2.3.5
huggingface_hub: 1.27.0
outlines: 0.1.11
xgrammar: 0.2.1
openai: 2.6.1
torchcodec: 0.11.1
ulimit soft: 1024
```

Comparison engine: **vLLM 0.28.0**, same node, same weights.

### Version note

Measured on v0.5.17. v0.5.19 declares `torch==2.13.0` and `flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.6.18`; this deployment is pinned to `torch 2.11.0+cu130` to match the training stack, and I did not want to report numbers from a hand-forced, unsupported combination. If you can confirm the intended torch/flashinfer pairing for v0.5.19 on H200, I'm glad to re-run the same comparison and post the numbers here.

items.title: [Bug] GLM-5.x NoPE MLA (qk_rope_head_dim=0) cannot run on SM120: every DSA sparse-MLA backend is unavailable
items.body:
## Summary

GLM-5.x uses **NoPE MLA**: `qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, so the absorbed query head dim is
`kv_lora_rank` (512) rather than the DeepSeek `512 + 64 = 576`.

On **SM120** (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, compute capability 12.0) this model cannot be served at
all. Every `--dsa-prefill-backend` / `--dsa-decode-backend` choice fails, each for a distinct
reason, and the one backend the code *forces* for GLM + fp8 KV + SM120 is the one whose
FlashInfer kernel rejects NoPE. So with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the model is unrunnable by
construction; with bf16 KV the remaining backends are each blocked as documented below.

This is not specific to any quantized/pruned repack — the geometry below comes from the model
config and applies to the full model too.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, SM120 (cc 12.0), 96 GB |
| Driver | 596.72 |
| OS | Windows 11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 |
| torch | 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0) |
| sglang | 0.5.19 |
| flashinfer | 0.6.18 |
| tilelang | 0.1.12 |
| nvcc | 13.4.59 |

Model (same geometry as the official GLM-5.3-Flash; observed on
`Asilarkness/GLM-5.3-Flash-Uncensored-NVFP4-Pruning-62GB`, a fingerprint-preserving repack):

```json
"architectures": ["Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration"],
"num_attention_heads": 64, "kv_lora_rank": 512,
"qk_nope_head_dim": 256, "qk_rope_head_dim": 0, "v_head_dim": 256,
"mla_use_nope": true, "index_topk": 2048
```

Note this matches flashinfer's own `nope_mla_dimensions` preset
(`qk_nope_head_dim=256, qk_rope_head_dim=0, v_head_dim=256, kv_lora_rank=512`) exactly, so NoPE
MLA is a first-class geometry upstream — just not on SM120.

## Device constraint (verified)

`cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` on this part is **101376 B (99 KB)**
(`sharedMemPerMultiprocessor` = 102400). Verified with a minimal CUDA program:
`cudaFuncSetAttribute(k, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, n)` returns
`invalid argument` for n ∈ {131072, 163840, 202752, 206848} and succeeds at 101376.
Hopper/B200 expose ~228 KB, which is the budget the kernels below are written against.

## Failure 1 — `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` (bf16 KV): needs 202 KB, device allows 99 KB

```
--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
```

```
File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/tilelang_kernel.py", line 1397, in tilelang_sparse_fwd
    out = kernel(q.unsqueeze(0), kv.unsqueeze(0), indices.unsqueeze(0))
  ...
tvm.error.InternalError: Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 206848
```

`tail_dim == 0` for NoPE, so this routes to `sparse_attention_fwd_kernel_v1`. Its shared
footprint with `num_heads=64, dim=512, block_I=64, bf16` is:

```
Q_shared     [64, 512] * 2 = 65536
KV_shared    [64, 512] * 2 = 65536
O_shared     [64, 512] * 2 = 65536
S_shared     [64,  64] * 2 =  8192
                             ------
                             204800   (+ padding -> the reported 206848)
```

Two observations:

1. **`O_shared` is dead.** It is written by `T.copy(acc_o, O_shared)` and never read — the very
   next line copies `acc_o` straight to `Output`. That is 64 KB allocated for nothing, and on
   SM120 it is fatal on its own (Q + O = 128 KB already exceeds the 99 KB opt-in ceiling).
2. Even without it, the default tile does not fit. The only remaining lever is the KV tile:
   `block_I=16` brings it to ~84 KB, but at that tile size tilelang's `LayoutInference` fails —
   the `acc_s`-derived reduction layouts (`m_i`, `sumexp_i`) can no longer be unified with the
   layouts of the scalars consumed by the `acc_o` loops (`alpha`, `sumexp`):

```
tvm.error.InternalError: Layout infer conflict between m_i and alpha in T.Parallel loop
tvm.error.InternalError: Layout infer conflict between sumexp_i and sumexp in T.Parallel loop
```

   (The same file's `sparse_attention_fwd_kernel_v2` sidesteps this class of conflict by keeping
   per-head scalars in shared memory — so v1 appears to rely on the default tile size to make
   the layouts line up.)

   We stopped at this point; shrinking the tile is a workaround, not a fix.

## Failure 2 — `--dsa-prefill-backend flashinfer_sparse_mla` (fp8 KV): kernel rejects NoPE

```
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --dsa-prefill-backend flashinfer_sparse_mla --dsa-decode-backend flashinfer_sparse_mla
```

```
ValueError: SM120 sparse MLA v32/GLM expects kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=64, and query
head dim 576; got kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=0, query dim=512
```
(`flashinfer/mla/_core.py:584-590`, in `_trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_v32_sm120`)

This is the important one, because `_validate_flashinfer_sparse_mla_backend`
(`sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_mla_sm120.py`, raised from
`sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py:519`) **requires** this backend for GLM DSA:

```python
is_glm_sm12_fp8 = (model_arch in _GLM_DSA_MODEL_ARCHS
                   and device_sm_major == 12
                   and kv_cache_dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn)
...
if is_glm_sm12_fp8:
    unsupported = selected - {"flashinfer_sparse_mla"}
    if unsupported:
        raise ValueError("GLM DSA with FP8 KV cache on NVIDIA SM120/SM121 supports only "
                         "flashinfer_sparse_mla, but got {...}")
```

`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` is in `_GLM_DSA_MODEL_ARCHS`. So for GLM + fp8 on SM120 the
user is locked to the single backend whose FlashInfer kernel requires the DeepSeek 576-wide
(nope 512 + rope 64) layout, while GLM-5.x is NoPE (512). The error text says "v32/**GLM**",
so this path is clearly intended to serve GLM — it just cannot serve a NoPE GLM.

## Failure 3 — `--dsa-*-backend trtllm`: the native NoPE path has no SM120 kernel

FlashInfer 0.6.18 *does* have a purpose-built NoPE sparse path — `_core.py:3786-3797`:

```python
is_nope_mla = (kv_lora_rank == nope_mla_dimensions.kv_lora_rank
               and qk_rope_head_dim == nope_mla_dimensions.qk_rope_head_dim)
if is_nope_mla and sparse_mla_top_k <= 0:
    raise ValueError("Native qk_rope_head_dim=0 TRTLLM-GEN MLA requires sparse_mla_top_k > 0")
if is_nope_mla and sparse_mla_top_k_lens is None:
    raise ValueError("Native qk_rope_head_dim=0 TRTLLM-GEN MLA requires sparse_mla_top_k_lens")
```

sglang feeds it correctly — `_forward_trtllm` comments "The BF16 no-RoPE path passes a
zero-width q_rope tensor" (`dsa_backend.py:3437`) and builds `sparse_mla_top_k_lens` via
`prepare_trtllm_nope_sparse_metadata` exactly when `qk_rope_head_dim == 0`. But the kernel:

```
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TllmGenFmhaRunner' at
.../flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37: Unsupported architecture
```

`backend="auto"` is no way out either: `_core.py:3833-3838` routes SM120 + `sparse_mla_top_k > 0`
to `backend="sparse"`, i.e. straight back to Failure 2.

## Failure 4 — remaining backends

* **`flashmla_kv` / `flashmla_sparse`** — `sglang/kernels/ops/attention/flash_mla_sm120.py`
  states it directly: *"On SM120 (Blackwell Desktop / RTX PRO 6000) the flash_mla CUDA kernel is
  not available"*.
* **`triton`** — `_triton_sparse_mla_fwd_single` / `_triton_sparse_mla_fwd_splitk`
  (`sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/triton_sparse_mla.py`) take the rope part as a
  `D_TAIL: tl.constexpr` and index it with `dt = tl.arange(0, D_TAIL)`; with NoPE the rope is
  zero-width, so this cannot be specialized. (This kernel is otherwise a good citizen here — it
  is the only one that adapts its `BLOCK_K` to the device's shared-memory limit.)
* **Dense MHA one-shot** — `set_dsa_prefill_impl` (`dsa_backend.py:3628-3642`) gates
  `MHA_ONE_SHOT` on `device_sm == 90 or (100 <= device_sm < 110) or _IS_GFX95`, so SM120 is
  excluded by design; and `_forward_standard_mha`'s `device_sm_major >= 10` branch calls
  `flashinfer.prefill.trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`, another trtllm-gen kernel.

## What we'd like

Any one of these would unblock SM120 serving for NoPE GLM:

1. Support `qk_rope_head_dim == 0` in the SM120 sparse MLA kernel
   (`sparse_mla_sm120_{prefill,decode}.cu` / `_sparse_mla_sm120.py`) — i.e. a 512-wide
   (nope-only) page layout. The Python gate at `_core.py:584` currently rejects it before the
   kernel is even reached, and `nope_mla_dimensions` already exists as a supported geometry.
2. Or let the `flashinfer_sparse_mla` validator fall back to the trtllm-gen NoPE path when
   available (and give that path an SM120 build — Failure 3).
3. Or make the tilelang v1 kernel SM120-safe: drop the dead `O_shared`, and size the tile from
   the device's actual `sharedMemPerBlockOptin` instead of assuming a ~228 KB budget (the
   triton kernel already does exactly this for `BLOCK_K`).

Happy to test any of these on the hardware above, and to run whatever diagnostic builds would
help — this GPU is available and the model is local.

items.title: [Feature] Interleaved Prefill Pipeline Parallelism for DeepSeek-V4.1: PP4 x CP2 with Two Virtual Stages per Rank
items.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Summary

Introduce forward-only interleaved pipeline parallelism for DeepSeek-V4.1 Prefill. Each physical PP rank owns two non-contiguous layer chunks: one from the first 20 layers and one from the last 20 layers.

This is physical **PP4 x CP2 with virtual pipeline size 2 (VPP2)**, using eight GPUs in total. It is not physical PP8.

The proposal separates:

1. Physical ranks and their communication groups.
2. Logical stages and their execution order.
3. Shared KV sources and their producer/consumer ownership.

Non-contiguous weight placement alone is insufficient. The design also requires a stage-aware scheduler, mHC state handoff, explicit shared-cache dependencies, and a coordinated cache/PD lifecycle.

## Motivation and Evidence

DeepSeek-V4.1's causal encoder-decoder (CED) structure and cross-layer sharing make equal layer counts a poor proxy for equal Prefill cost. Splitting layers 0-19 and 20-39 is semantically possible, but can be poorly balanced, especially with decoder SWA bounded replay:

- The early layers process the full uncached extend.
- Layer 20 still processes the full extend and produces shared C1 KV and candidate information.
- Layers 21-39 can process only the bounded replay tail.
- Engram at layers 1 and 14 and source-layer projections add uneven costs.

Pairing an early and a late chunk on each physical rank may balance these costs across concurrent microbatches. It does not make late layers independent of early layers, and does not guarantee lower single-request TTFT.

Relevant limitations in this baseline:

- `make_layers()` and `get_pp_indices()` describe one contiguous layer interval per physical rank.
- `DeepseekV4Model`'s pre-mix mHC path rejects PP and initializes its previous pre-mix state at model entry.
- The CP-v2 eager runner starts with embedding/sharding; it needs a non-first-logical-stage path.
- The PP scheduler uses physical first/last-rank checks to determine activation, output, and completion handling.
- Compressed-pool source lookup is restricted to the current contiguous stage.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 feature validation rejects PP.

## Goals and Non-Goals

### Goals

- Support the concrete PP4 x CP2 / VPP2 topology below.
- Preserve existing V4.1 model semantics without recomputing source layers at consumers.
- Preserve CP-local activation handoff, mHC state, and global logical token identity.
- Support explicit cross-stage compressed-KV, Indexer-K, Top-k, and candidate dependencies.
- Integrate with Prefill prefix caching and Mooncake PD into a non-speculative Decode worker.
- Provide bounded memory, deterministic scheduling, cancellation, and measurable performance.

### Non-goals for the first implementation

- PP + DSpark, MTP, or other speculative algorithms on either PD peer.
- Decode-side VPP, Decode CP/DCP, DP > 1, mixed Prefill/Decode scheduling, or multimodal requests.
- Arbitrary layer placement and automatic topology search.
- Encoder SWA bounded replay.
- HiCache/L3, NIXL, and CUDA graph capture for the new VPP execution path.
- Guaranteed speedup or a claim that five-layer chunks are optimal.

Decoder SWA bounded replay is a follow-up milestone, not a prerequisite for the first correctness implementation. The initial path should run eager Prefill with both bounded-replay modes disabled.

## Topology and Terminology

All layer IDs are zero-based; ranges below are inclusive.

| Physical PP rank | CP lanes | Virtual chunk 0 | Virtual chunk 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PP0 | CP0, CP1 | Stage 0: L0-L4 | Stage 4: L20-L24 |
| PP1 | CP0, CP1 | Stage 1: L5-L9 | Stage 5: L25-L29 |
| PP2 | CP0, CP1 | Stage 2: L10-L14 | Stage 6: L30-L34 |
| PP3 | CP0, CP1 | Stage 3: L15-L19 | Stage 7: L35-L39 |

```text
Logical execution:  S0 -> S1 -> S2 -> S3 -> S4 -> S5 -> S6 -> S7
Physical placement: P0 -> P1 -> P2 -> P3 -> P0 -> P1 -> P2 -> P3

Each activation edge preserves CP lane:
  (source physical rank, CP0) -> (destination physical rank, CP0)
  (source physical rank, CP1) -> (destination physical rank, CP1)
```

A request must finish S3 before executing S4. P0 must not execute L20 immediately after L4 for that request. Multiple microbatches provide overlap between the two local chunks.

The topology corresponds conceptually to the existing physical knobs `--tp 2 --attn-cp-size 2 --pp-size 4` with DP1, plus a **new, proposed** virtual-pipeline layout option. This is not a runnable VPP launch command today. Here SGLang's `tp_size=2` is the width of each PP stage; effective attention TP is 1. EP is a separate model-parallel choice within that width.

Physical placement should keep each CP pair on a fast local link and account for the P3-to-P0 wraparound. One eight-GPU node and multi-node placements need separate measurements; the layer map does not prescribe node placement.

## Cross-Stage Dependencies

The dependency planner must resolve global source IDs before filtering layers by physical ownership.

| Source | Consumer range | Required remote destinations in this mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C2 KV and Indexer K from L2 | L2-L7 | PP1 |
| C2 KV and Indexer K from L8 | L8-L13 | PP2 |
| C2 KV and Indexer K from L14 | L14-L19 | PP3 |
| C1 KV and Indexer K from L20 | L20-L39 | PP1, PP2, PP3 |
| Candidate information from L20 | Subsequent candidate-consuming indexers | PP1, PP2, PP3 |
| Selected Top-k at index-source layers | Subsequent layers until the next index source | Only stage edges crossing that reuse interval |

Indexer source layers are L2, L8, L14, L20, L24, L28, L32, and L36. The planner should derive exact dependencies from the model configuration rather than hard-code this table.

For example, S4 ends at L24 while S5 starts at L25. S5 requires L24's selected positions before its next index source at L28. Similarly, S6 initially uses L28's result and S7 initially uses L32's result.

Each target layer owns its own SWA computation/storage. Consumer stages need the shared compressed history, not another layer's SWA cache. C2 pending pair state remains at its compressor producer for continuation; it is not broadcast to attention-only consumers. It may still require producer-owned handoff to Decode under the PD protocol.

## Proposed Architecture

### A. One immutable pipeline layout

Introduce a `PipelineLayout` with:

- Ordered logical-stage ranges and their physical owners.
- Per-rank `owned_layer_ids` and per-stage `execution_layer_ids`.
- Global KV/index/candidate source dependency maps.
- Protocol/layout version and a stable manifest digest.

Startup validation must establish that every target layer executes exactly once, execution preserves model order, dependencies point to valid upstream producers, and all ranks agree on the same manifest. Reject unsupported source dependencies rather than silently changing the model.

For this particular mapping:

```text
logical_stage_id = virtual_chunk_id * physical_pp_size + physical_pp_rank
owned_layer_ids(PP0) = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24]
```

These are proposed interface semantics, not existing SGLang APIs.

### B. Stage-aware model execution

Keep checkpoint-visible absolute layer names. A global-indexed module list can retain `PPMissingLayer` entries for non-owned layers, while an explicit ownership-aware construction helper instantiates only the two owned chunks. Preserve the existing contiguous helper for ordinary PP.

Expose an explicit stage execution contract such as:

```text
forward_stage(stage_id, execution_context, pp_proxy_tensors) -> stage_result
```

Requirements:

- Only S0 performs embedding and initial CP hidden sharding.
- Subsequent stages consume received CP-local hidden directly; never shard it a second time.
- Preserve the existing three-dimensional mHC semantics, even if the wire representation is flattened.
- Carry `prev_pre` with hidden across each logical boundary; do not reset it at the second local chunk.
- Only S7 performs final mHC combine, final normalization, CP output gathering, logits, and sampling.
- Retain full logical token/position metadata needed by Engram hashing; hashing a CP-local token stream would lose n-gram predecessors.
- Audit loaders, offloaders, layer enumeration, pool sizing, and layer-ready counters for contiguous-range assumptions.

Do not temporarily mutate the global PP group's first/last-rank identity. Logical stage entry/exit and physical rank identity serve different purposes and must remain explicit.

### C. Forward-only interleaved scheduler

Add an opt-in Prefill VPP execution path instead of modifying the existing loop by replacing `pp_size` with 8.

An execution task is identified by `(microbatch_id, generation, logical_stage_id)`. Generation prevents late messages for a recycled slot from being accepted by a new request.

Proposed task lifecycle:

```text
planned -> waiting_dependencies -> ready -> running -> sending -> retired
                                                   \-> cancelling -> drained
```

Separate compute readiness from buffer retirement: a stage may have computed its result while its activation/cache sends are still in flight.

Initially allow one microbatch to traverse all eight stages. This validates semantics but is not a throughput implementation. Then introduce bounded ready queues and overlapping microbatches, with downstream/backpressure-aware arbitration and fairness between the two local chunks.

All CP lanes of one physical stage must execute the same logical task sequence. A leader/consensus schedule should publish that sequence; independent rank-local arrival order is unsafe for collectives. Do not apply a training 1F1B schedule: this is inference, without backward passes.

The first visit allocates the request's local resources. The second visit reuses them. It must not allocate the request twice, count the prompt twice, sample twice, or release resources after the first chunk.

### D. Typed asynchronous communication

Use typed envelopes with at least:

```text
protocol_version, layout_digest, microbatch_id, generation
src_stage, dst_stage, message_kind, tensor_schema, token_layout_id
```

Message kinds:

- `activation`: CP-local hidden and mHC `prev_pre`.
- `cache_update`: committed source KV/Indexer-K ranges or pages.
- `index_state`: logical selected positions and compact candidate information.
- `completion` / `cancel`: control-plane lifecycle events.

S3-to-S4 activation and S7 completion both involve the last physical rank but must never be confused. Reuse transport primitives where possible, not physical-first/last control-flow assumptions.

Prepost or otherwise schedule receives with bounded sends to avoid cyclic wait at the wraparound. Explicit CUDA events order producer writes, transport reads, destination installation, and consumer reads. Buffers are released only after all readers and send handles complete. A message header alone does not ensure NCCL ordering; define and test collective/P2P launch ordering across streams and CP lanes.

### E. Two-level state ownership

| Category | Examples | Owner and lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execution-scoped intermediate state | hidden, `prev_pre`, query-specific Top-k/candidates, tail layout | One microbatch/stage execution; release after consumers and sends complete |
| Content-scoped committed cache | compressed KV, Indexer K, valid layer-specific paged SWA | Prefix/source identity; reusable while resident and valid |
| Request-scoped continuation state | incomplete C2 pair/ring and allocation mappings | Producer request lifecycle; snapshot/release explicitly |

Do not permanently attach scratch buffers to request slots. Paged SWA can be content-stable; it must not be conflated with the request-scoped C2 ring.

For source caches, maintain separate producer-owned and consumer-replica registries:

- A producer computes each source once.
- A consumer has local storage/mapping for remote sources required by its layers.
- Prefix identity, source ID, model/format identity, residency generation, and valid installed ranges determine replica usability.
- Transfer only missing ranges; install data before advancing the valid frontier.
- Each request maps logical positions to its own physical slots.
- Top-k crosses ranks as logical compressed positions, not raw producer physical addresses.

The simplest first implementation can establish cold-request replicas and block on dependency completion. Warm-prefix delta synchronization should follow with explicit residency acknowledgements. Prefer forwarding/pipelining source ranges to downstream consumers over sending full histories at every microbatch.

### F. Prefix-cache admission and consistency

An upstream hit does not imply that downstream replicas or layer-specific SWA are available. A prefix is reusable only if every necessary local computation source can be recovered on every owning/consuming stage.

Gather stage-local cache readiness under a consistent logical prefix:

1. Determine the candidate content match.
2. Check target-layer SWA and producer/consumer source-cache availability.
3. Choose a common reusable boundary, or plan explicit replica restoration.
4. Lock participating cache entries before admission; avoid evicting a replica between checking and using it.
5. Resume computation only after required transfers/restores are ready.

A minimum across scalar frontiers is valid only if each frontier represents a contiguous, dependency-complete prefix. Arbitrary holes require range-aware readiness.

Keep token accounting global. CP-local query counts and VPP stage visits must not become prompt lengths. Request allocations and release ownership must be consistent within a physical stage; physical slot IDs need not be equal across stages.

HiCache is deferred until the device-resident contract works. It must eventually preserve this same source/layer manifest and restore-readiness protocol.

### G. PD integration

Initially use Mooncake with non-speculative Prefill and Decode. Decode can remain ordinary PP1/CP1; validate attention widths and buffer formats explicitly.

PD registration must enumerate typed absolute identities, e.g. `(buffer_kind, source_layer_id, format_version)`, rather than infer ownership from a contiguous start/end range or pointer count.

- Each source producer sends its canonical compressed KV/Indexer K.
- Each physical PP rank sends SWA for its owned target layers.
- Consumer replicas are not duplicate PD sources.
- C2 continuation state is sent from its producer according to the target-only PD contract.
- Within a producer's CP group, partition replicated KV pages among senders or elect a sender per range; do not send duplicate copies to the same destination address.
- Decode waits for the complete required manifest and final output handoff, not merely the last logical stage.
- Prefill resources remain protected until all PP consumers and PD readers complete.

This target-only layout needs independent validation; it must not depend on the existing DSpark-specific bootstrap fingerprint being present.

## Communication Budget

Assumptions: BF16 mHC hidden, hidden size 5120, mHC multiplier 4, 512 selected INT32 indices, 32K = 32768 uncached tokens in one example request. Values are logical payload estimates, not measured network traffic.

| Payload | Approximate bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| mHC hidden per query token | 5120 x 4 x 2 = 40960 B = 40 KiB |
| `prev_pre` per query, assuming four FP32 coefficients | 16 B |
| Compressed KV row | 584 B |
| Indexer K row with scales | 68 B |
| Selected Top-k per query when needed across an edge | 512 x 4 = 2048 B |

With bounded replay disabled:

- One full activation handoff: 1.25 GiB; two CP lanes carry about 640 MiB each.
- Ordinary four-stage contiguous PP: three activation boundaries, 3.75 GiB cumulative.
- The proposed eight-stage mapping: seven boundaries, 8.75 GiB cumulative.

These totals exclude internal CP collectives, PD transfer, page padding, protocol headers, candidate traffic, and avoidable replicated sends. They are not link latency estimates.

Required compressed KV + Indexer-K copies for a cold request:

```text
C2: three sources, each with N/2 rows copied to one remote consumer
C1: one source with N rows copied to three remote consumers
Total = (3N/2 + 3N) * (584 + 68)
      ~= 91.7 MiB at N = 32768
```

This assumes one logical copy per destination physical stage with local CP replication; naive per-lane duplicate transfers can increase traffic. Warm-prefix copies depend on downstream residency, not only on upstream hits.

With decoder bounded replay, the first four activation boundaries carry the full extend and the last three carry a 128-token tail in the single-request example: about 5.01 GiB of hidden payload. Shared historical C1 keys can still be required after the tail switch.

Do not transmit dense query-by-context scores or byte-per-position candidate masks. Prefer logical Top-k and compact block IDs/bitsets selected for the actual context and candidate density. Packing format and rank-local row alignment require a versioned contract.

## Decoder Bounded Replay Follow-up

The proposed split places L20 inside S4:

- S0-S3 process the full uncached extend.
- S4 executes L20 over the full extend, then switches L21-L24 to the replay tail.
- S5-S7 process the same tail layout.

Carry explicit full/tail layout identity, original token indices, positions, per-request local lengths, and CP padding/gather metadata. All stages must agree on which logical rows those tensors represent.

The metadata must be execution-local and must survive interleaving without overwriting another microbatch's candidate masks or attention buffers. Final logits must use the matching tail metadata without relying on DSpark auxiliary capture.

Tail queries may still read full historical compressed keys; bounded query execution does not imply bounded source-cache transfer.

## Alternatives and Trade-offs

| Alternative | Benefit | Cost / reason not selected as the primary design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing CP-only Prefill | No PP activation traffic; simplest baseline | Limited per-device weight capacity; no layer pipeline |
| Contiguous PP2 at L20 | Keeps major shared-source groups local | CED/replay and Engram imbalance |
| Unequal contiguous PP4 | Fewer activation edges; potentially good balance | May still cross source groups; should be benchmarked, not dismissed |
| Proposed PP4/CP2/VPP2 | Pairs early/late work; distributes Engram layers | Seven activation edges, wraparound, more scheduler and cache complexity |
| Recompute upstream sources on consumers | Less explicit source-cache synchronization | Requires upstream inputs/weights or recomputation; risks duplicating expensive work |

VPP2 is a candidate, not a predetermined performance winner. Five-layer partitions simplify discussion; profile-guided boundaries may be better. With eight GPUs fixed, CP8 and PP4 x CP2 use different per-stage CP widths. A speedup must not be attributed solely to VPP without an equal-GPU comparison.

## Implementation Plan and Acceptance

1. **Layout and ownership:** immutable manifest, two local chunks, global checkpoint names, correct per-rank weight and pool enumeration; reject invalid source graphs.
2. **Serial correctness:** one microbatch through eight stages, CP-local activation and `prev_pre` handoff, reference parity; speculative decoding and both replay modes off.
3. **Shared-cache correctness:** cold replica installation, Top-k remapping, then warm-prefix restore/delta protocol and source-aware admission.
4. **Interleaved execution:** bounded queues, backpressure, deterministic CP scheduling, stream/event lifetimes, cancellation and failure cleanup.
5. **PD integration:** typed source manifest, per-layer SWA ownership, transfer completion and release coordination.
6. **Decoder replay and tuning:** explicit tail metadata, workload-aware stage balance and communication overlap.

Required tests:

- Invalid layouts, duplicated/missing layers, source/consumer dependency resolution, and VPP1 compatibility.
- CP lanes with uneven or empty local rows; batches with mixed lengths and prefixes.
- Chunk boundaries around odd/even C2 pairs, source boundaries, page boundaries, and the S3-to-S4 wrap.
- Logical-to-physical index remapping with deliberately different pool slots on each stage.
- Cold cache, identical warm prefix, branching prefixes, consumer-replica eviction, and restore under pressure.
- Interleaved microbatches with different layouts; stale generation messages, cancelled requests, failed transfers, and bounded resource reclamation.
- Logits/top-k agreement against the non-VPP reference within pre-agreed backend numerical tolerances; task-level quality evaluation where numerical differences affect selection.
- PD Decode sees every required source and correct SWA/C2 state before the first step.

Performance evaluation should use equal GPU counts and identical model, dtype, EP policy, caching and replay settings:

- Compare CP8, feasible contiguous PP variants, and PP4 x CP2/VPP2.
- Measure cold prompts at 4K/32K/128K and warm long prefixes with short extends, including approximately 64 new tokens.
- Report end-to-end TTFT p50/p95, logical uncached-token throughput, stage compute time, dependency/communication wait, pipeline idle time, peak memory, and PP/CP/PD bytes separately.
- Sweep microbatch depth and report both throughput and latency. Do not treat page-rounded scheduler token budgets or internal post-insert cache rematches as request-level work/hit measurements.

No VPP prototype or speedup result is claimed in this RFC. Existing CP/PD tests and deployment logs are not evidence of VPP correctness.

## Failure Handling, Compatibility, and Rollout

The feature is opt-in. Existing PP and VPP1 behavior remain unchanged. A new virtual-size/layout option is proposed, with final CLI naming left to maintainers.

Validate peer manifests before exchanging pointers or entering data-plane collectives. On timeout, layout mismatch, or stale generation, fail the affected execution and coordinate draining; do not locally requeue one CP lane. If the transport cannot safely recover, fail/restart the engine rather than reuse in-flight storage.

Canary rollout should follow correctness and pressure testing. Stop rollout on output regressions, rank divergence, unbounded memory, stuck dependency queues, or unacceptable latency regressions. Roll back by draining requests, restarting on the existing CP-only/non-VPP recipe, and rebuilding caches. Do not reinterpret VPP cache state under a different layout.

Logs and metrics should carry opaque execution IDs, stage IDs and lengths, not prompt text or KV contents. Any experimental residency-debug logging should be bounded and removed or gated before general deployment.

items.title: [Bug] DP scheduler rank can permanently stop processing requests after a near-KV-capacity request is cancelled
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

A request whose input length is close to the KV cache capacity can pass request validation but can never be admitted by `PrefillAdder`.

This can permanently block the affected scheduler rank after the request is cancelled. The problem is in CPU-side scheduler admission and state management, so it can be reproduced without a GPU or model execution.

The production configuration that originally exposed the problem had:

- KV capacity per DP rank: 190,784 tokens
- Page size: 64
- Advertised maximum input threshold: 190,778 tokens
- Stable triggering input range: 190,720–190,777 tokens

For these requests, `init_req_max_new_tokens()` clips `max_new_tokens` to zero. However, `PrefillAdder` additionally reserves one allocator page and requires:

`input_length + max_new_tokens + page_size < available_kv_tokens`

For an input length of 190,720:

`190720 + 0 + 64 >= 190784`

The request therefore returns `NO_TOKEN` and is not added to `PrefillAdder.can_run_list`, even though it passed the public input-length validation.

The scheduler then persists `running_batch.batch_is_full=True`. On later scheduling iterations, `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw()` checks this flag before traversing the waiting queue and returns early.

After the problematic request is cancelled:

- the waiting request is removed,
- the running batch is empty,
- KV usage is zero,

but `batch_is_full` remains `True`. A short follow-up request routed to the same scheduler rank is never considered, and subsequent requests remain queued indefinitely.

Restarting the server is the only observed recovery method.

Expected behavior:

- Requests that can never satisfy `PrefillAdder` admission should be rejected at request intake.
- `batch_is_full` should be invalidated after the running batch becomes empty.
- Cancelling one request must not permanently block future requests on that scheduler rank.

### Reproduction

The following state-level reproduction uses the real SGLang request validation, `PrefillAdder`, and scheduler prefill loop. It does not require a GPU or model weights.

Checkout the affected revision:

```bash
git checkout ec5fba577
```

Create an isolated CPU test environment with `uv`:

```bash
uv venv --python /usr/bin/python3.12 .venv

uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python \
  torch==2.13.0 \
  torchvision==0.28.0 \
  numpy \
  psutil \
  packaging \
  requests \
  pyzmq \
  setproctitle \
  msgspec \
  orjson \
  fastapi \
  uvicorn \
  uvloop \
  pydantic \
  python-multipart \
  aiohttp \
  anthropic \
  openai==2.6.1 \
  tiktoken \
  pillow \
  transformers==5.12.1 \
  tokenizers==0.22.2 \
  huggingface-hub \
  interegular \
  partial-json-parser \
  sentencepiece \
  scipy \
  einops \
  tqdm \
  xxhash \
  zstandard \
  pybase64 \
  prometheus-client \
  IPython \
  dill \
  compressed-tensors==0.18.0 \
  gguf \
  xgrammar==0.2.1 \
  setuptools-scm \
  setuptools-rust \
  wheel

SGLANG_BUILD_RUST_EXTS=none uv pip install \
  --python .venv/bin/python \
  --no-deps \
  --no-build-isolation \
  --editable ./python
```

Save the following as `repro_dp_hang_cpu.py`:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req
from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy import AddReqResult, PrefillAdder
from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
from sglang.srt.managers.utils import validate_input_length
from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import (
    DecLockRefResult,
    IncLockRefResult,
)


capacity = 190_784
page_size = 64
input_len = 190_720

# get_worker_info() previously advertised max_req_len - 5.
public_threshold = capacity - 6

req = MagicMock(spec=Req)
req.rid = "near-capacity"
req.origin_input_ids = list(range(input_len))
req.full_untruncated_fill_ids = list(range(input_len))
req.prefix_indices = []
req.output_ids = []
req.sampling_params = SimpleNamespace(
    max_new_tokens=0,
    ignore_eos=False,
)
req.retracted_stain = False
req.host_hit_length = 0
req.storage_hit_length = 0
req.storage_hit_start = None
req.host_hit_is_storage = False
req.host_loaded_length = 0
req.last_node = MagicMock()
req.needs_host_load_back.return_value = False

validation_error = validate_input_length(
    req,
    public_threshold,
    allow_auto_truncate=False,
)

tree_cache = MagicMock()
tree_cache.disable = False
tree_cache.supports_mamba.return_value = False
tree_cache.evictable_size.return_value = 0
tree_cache.full_evictable_size.return_value = 0
tree_cache.inc_lock_ref.return_value = IncLockRefResult()
tree_cache.dec_lock_ref.return_value = DecLockRefResult()

allocator = MagicMock()
allocator.available_size.return_value = capacity

running_for_adder = MagicMock()
running_for_adder.reqs = []

adder = PrefillAdder(
    page_size=page_size,
    tree_cache=tree_cache,
    token_to_kv_pool_allocator=allocator,
    running_batch=running_for_adder,
    new_token_ratio=1.0,
    rem_input_tokens=capacity,
    rem_chunk_tokens=None,
)

result = adder.add_one_req(
    req,
    has_chunked_req=False,
    truncation_align_size=None,
)

# Reproduce the state after NO_TOKEN, cancellation of the long request,
# and arrival of a short follow-up request.
scheduler = object.__new__(Scheduler)
scheduler.grammar_manager = SimpleNamespace(
    has_waiting_grammars=lambda: False
)
scheduler.enable_hierarchical_cache = False
scheduler.enable_unified_cache_external_linker = False
scheduler.enable_priority_preemption = False
scheduler.is_hybrid_swa = False
scheduler.chunked_req = None
scheduler.waiting_queue = [
    SimpleNamespace(rid="short-follow-up"),
]

empty_running_batch = SimpleNamespace(
    batch_is_full=(result == AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN),
    is_empty=lambda: True,
)

with patch(
    "sglang.srt.managers.scheduler.get_memory",
    return_value=SimpleNamespace(enable_flexkv=False),
):
    batch_to_run, _ = Scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw(
        scheduler,
        None,
        empty_running_batch,
    )

print(f"public_threshold={public_threshold}")
print(
    "input_validation="
    f"{'accepted' if validation_error is None else 'rejected'}"
)
print(f"prefill_result={result.name}")
print(f"request_admitted={req in adder.can_run_list}")
print(f"follow_up_scheduled={batch_to_run is not None}")
print(
    "batch_is_full_after_empty_iteration="
    f"{empty_running_batch.batch_is_full}"
)

assert validation_error is None
assert result == AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN
assert req not in adder.can_run_list
assert batch_to_run is None
assert empty_running_batch.batch_is_full

print("BUG_REPRODUCED")
```

Run it:

```bash
.venv/bin/python repro_dp_hang_cpu.py
```

Output on `main@ec5fba577`:

```text
public_threshold=190778
input_validation=accepted
prefill_result=NO_TOKEN
request_admitted=False
follow_up_scheduled=False
batch_is_full_after_empty_iteration=True
BUG_REPRODUCED
```

A sweep of the original triggering interval produced the same admission mismatch for all 58 input lengths from 190,720 through 190,777.

For comparison, the proposed fix changes the effective threshold to 190,720 and clears the stale state after the running batch becomes empty:

```text
public_threshold=190720
input_validation=rejected
prefill_result=NO_TOKEN
request_admitted=False
batch_is_full_after_empty_iteration=False
FIX_CONFIRMED
```

The relevant unit tests also pass in the same CPU-only environment:

```text
43 passed, 17 warnings, 558 subtests passed
```

This state-level reproduction does not load or execute any model. It directly exercises the CPU-side scheduler admission and stale-state logic using mocked KV/cache objects.

### Environment

`torch.cuda.is_available()` returned `False`.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 SM120 decode pads q to 64 heads for an SM90 constraint; removing the pad changes greedy output despite the kernel being bit-identical
items.body:
### Summary

On SM120/121, DeepSeek-V4 decode pads `q` to 64 heads even when the rank owns fewer and
FlashInfer has an instance for the real count. Removing the pad is worth **0.50% of a
decode step** at TP4 — small, and I would not open a PR for it on its own.

What I would like a second opinion on is that removing it **changes greedy output**, which
should be impossible if the padded heads are inert. The comment in the padding block says
they are not, so this may be known and intentional — but then the constraint is stronger
than the one the code cites, and it is worth writing down.

### The padding

`srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` (around line 1886):

```python
skip_decode_pad = is_sm120_supported() and x.shape[0] > SM120_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS
padded_num_heads = (self.n_local_heads if skip_decode_pad
                    else (64 if self.n_local_heads <= 64 else self.n_heads))
```

with the reason given just below:

```
# FlashMLA's fp8 sparse decode kernel only specializes h_q for {64, 128}.
```

That is the SM90 `sgl_kernel` FlashMLA constraint. On the SM120 path the kernel is
FlashInfer's `sparse_mla_sm120`, whose `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` carries
`{8, 16, 32, 64, 128} x {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024}` and which exports
`_decode_dsv4_dispatchable(num_tokens, num_heads, topk, d_qk, page_block_size, extra_topk)`
for exactly this question. At `num_attention_heads = 64` and attn-TP 4 each rank owns 16,
`(16, 512)` is in the table, so decode attends on 64 heads where 16 would do. Prefill
already skips the pad (`x.shape[0] > 64`), so only decode pays.

### Measured cost

4x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP4/EP2, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, concurrency 1, live traces from
`/start_profile` over a 41-step window, patched against unpatched:

| | padded to 64 | real 16 heads |
|---|---:|---:|
| `sparse_mla_decode_dsv4_kernel` | 25.3 us/call | 19.6 us/call |
| `sparse_mla_decode_dsv4_merge_kernel` | 3.7 us/call | 3.0 us/call |
| writing `q_out` | 2.1 us (strided `elementwise_kernel`) | 1.0 us (`memcpy32_post`) |
| **whole path** | **1.223 ms/step** | **0.915 ms/step** |

0.31 ms out of a 61.3 ms step. The third row is incidental but real: with the pad,
`q_out = q_padded[:, 0:16, :]` is non-contiguous, so the write is a strided copy kernel
instead of a memcpy.

A kernel-level A/B on an idle card suggested 2.3-3.2x and 1.37 ms/step. That was
over-optimistic by 4.4x: my synthetic `indices` were uniform random, which destroys KV
page locality, and made the 64-head kernel 58.4 us/call against the 25.3 it actually takes
in production. Quoting the trace, not the microbenchmark.

### The part I cannot explain

Removing the pad changes greedy output, reproducibly:

```
two unpatched boots, steady state, 4 prompts, temperature 0:  4/4 identical  (noise floor is zero)
patched boot vs either unpatched boot:                        1/4 identical
patched boot against itself:                                  4/4 identical
```

(Measured after discarding the first run of each boot — on this stack the first run after a
boot differs from steady state, which appears to be FlashInfer autotuning during it.)

Yet the kernel is bit-identical in isolation. Calling
`sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` directly at the production shapes (M=6, topk=512,
extra_topk=128, num_splits=10) and comparing `output[:, :16, :]` between h_q=64 and
h_q=16 gives **0 of 49152 elements different, max |difference| 0.000e+00** — and that holds
across every `chunks_per_block` from 1 to 10, with `attn_sink=None`, with a 64-long sink,
and with a 16-long sink. In the 64-head arm I filled heads 16-63 with *random* values
rather than zeros, and the first 16 heads still came out bit-identical, so the padded heads
do not appear to leak into the real ones at that shape.

A kernel inventory diff of the two traces shows the change is contained: 0 of 299 shared
(kernel, grid, block) entries changed call counts. The only entries that differ are the
sparse MLA kernels themselves, the `new_zeros` fill of the q buffer, and the q write
discussed above. Nothing else in the model ran differently.

So the output changes, and I cannot find where. Which brings me to the comment a few lines
below the dispatch:

```python
# The kernel reads all padded heads; uninitialized values can affect real-head
# outputs, so the padding must be zero even though only real heads are written.
```

If padded heads can affect real-head outputs, the pad is load-bearing in a way the
`{64, 128}` specialization comment does not capture, and the dispatch-table check would not
be a safe replacement for it. If they cannot, then something else in the decode path
depends on `q.shape[1]`, and I would like to know what.

### Questions

1. Is the 64-head pad still required on the SM120 path, given `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH`
   covers `(16, topk)`?
2. What is the "uninitialized values can affect real-head outputs" comment protecting
   against — is it about NaN/Inf specifically, or a genuine cross-head dependence?
3. Is there anything else in the decode path keyed on the padded head count that would
   change results?

Happy to run further experiments on this fleet; it is a 4x GB10 TP4 setup that reproduces
deterministically in steady state, which makes it a reasonable place to test this.

### Environment

- SGLang serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 / EP2, attn-TP 4, DSpark speculative decode
- FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUDA 13, 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121)

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + Engram: profiled SPS table (compact ragged verify) dies in CUDA-graph capture with "engram target-verify expects one equal block per request"
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (an Engram model), enabling DSpark compact ragged verify via a profiled SPS cost table makes the engine die **deterministically during CUDA-graph capture, on every rank**:

```
AssertionError: engram target-verify expects one equal block per request, got 42 tokens for 8 requests of 6
```

Removing the table (so the planner stays on the verify-all / static schedule) boots and serves fine, so weights, TP4/EP4, FP8 KV cache and the RDMA transport are all healthy.

**Suspected root cause.** The capture batch seems to get the wrong slot count. `DecodeCudaGraphRunner._ragged_capture_slots()` returns `min(num_tokens, self.max_bs)` (`model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:667-670`), while the per-tier token bucket is `bs * captured_req_width` (`_build_ragged_verify_token_buckets`, same file, line 569). items.title: [Bug] HiCacheFile reports an unrestorable prefix for hybrid cache pools
items.body:
## Describe the bug

`HiCacheFile.batch_exists_v2()` can report a hybrid prefix as a hit even when a required auxiliary pool cannot restore that prefix.

The file backend finds each pool's longest usable prefix and takes the minimum of those lengths. That works for contiguous `ALL_PAGES` coverage, but `TRAILING_PAGES` pools can have holes in their valid endpoints. For example, with all three KV pages present:

| SWA valid endpoints | Mamba valid endpoints | Expected shared endpoint | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{3}` | `{3}` | 3 | 3 |
| `{3}` | `{2}` | 0 (no common endpoint) | 2 |
| `{1, 3}` | `{1, 2}` | 1 | 2 |

In the latter two cases, the reported endpoint has no SWA object. The last case also overlooks an earlier valid common checkpoint. The same problem occurs when an `ALL_PAGES` pool truncates a trailing pool to an endpoint that the trailing pool cannot serve.

The usable prefix should end at the greatest common legal endpoint, or zero if none exists. `MooncakeStore.batch_exists_v2()` already uses an intersection of legal endpoints.

This report establishes an incorrect backend existence-query result. It does not claim a reproduced model-output error or an end-to-end load-back failure. It is separate from #38452, which concerns whether the scheduler consults L3.

## Reproduction

Run this in a source checkout with SGLang's Python dependencies available. No model, server, accelerator or valid KV payload is needed: empty temporary files are sufficient for the existence-query contract. The constructor is bypassed to isolate the query from unrelated eviction setup; the query and filesystem scan methods are unmodified.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import (
    HiCacheFile, PoolHitPolicy, PoolName, PoolTransfer,
)

def query(swa_pages, mamba_pages):
    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        backend = HiCacheFile.__new__(HiCacheFile)
        backend.file_path = directory
        backend.config_suffix = "_repro"
        backend.metadata_cache = None
        keys = ["p1", "p2", "p3"]
        for name, pages in (
            (PoolName.KV, {1, 2, 3}),
            (PoolName.SWA, swa_pages),
            (PoolName.MAMBA, mamba_pages),
        ):
            for page in pages:
                Path(backend._get_component_path(keys[page - 1], name)).touch()
        transfers = [
            PoolTransfer(
                name=name, keys=[keys[-1]],
                hit_policy=PoolHitPolicy.TRAILING_PAGES,
            )
            for name in (PoolName.SWA, PoolName.MAMBA)
        ]
        return backend.batch_exists_v2(keys, transfers).kv_hit_pages

actual = [query({3}, {3}), query({3}, {2}), query({1, 3}, {1, 2})]
print(actual)  # affected code: [3, 2, 2]
assert actual == [3, 0, 1]
```

## Environment

- Reproduced against `f618022b73f813daa6f25e615b0269c82c66a941`; the affected method is unchanged at `5f3606c7b2aec653fcfdbe3465379e700c4a5492`.
- macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon; Python 3.12.14; CPU Torch 2.13.0.
- Local validation imported the actual storage/environ modules through namespace packages to bypass SGLang's GPU-heavy package initialization. No storage-query method was replaced or extracted.
- Normal `python -m sglang.check_env` stops during package initialization with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'triton'`; therefore a full runtime environment report and GPU E2E result are not available.

I have a focused fix and CPU regression coverage ready. AI assistance was used for investigation and implementation.

items.title: [Feature] TRTLLM MLA target verification misses fused FP8 KV/Q preparation in forward_extend
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Problem

In our pinned SGLang v0.5.18-based build, the FP8 target-verification path in
`TRTLLMMLABackend.forward_extend()` does not use the fused KV/Q preparation
already available to `forward_decode()`.

Although speculative verification processes only a few new tokens, it dispatches
through `forward_extend()`. When `cos_sin_cache is None`, its preparation is:

1. Concatenate absorbed Q-nope and Q-rope.
2. Cast the concatenated Q, K-nope, and K-rope to FP8 (three casts).
3. Scatter the new KV rows into the persistent cache.

That is five kernel launches per MLA layer instead of one. This report concerns
target verification, not ordinary prefill or the separate fused-RoPE path.

Relevant code: [TRTLLM MLA backend](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mla_backend.py)
and [MLA preparation utilities](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/utils.py).
Those are navigation links; the measurements below are from our pinned build,
not a pristine current-main reproduction.

## Proposed change

Have decode and target-verify extend use the same guarded fused preparation
helper. Consume its returned FP8 query and skip the subsequent KV write when
fusion succeeds. Preserve fallback behavior for unsupported layouts, async
asserts, unavailable write locations, and paths requiring RoPE application.

We tested a stride-aware Triton implementation behind the shared FP8 entry
point, with architecture-gated PDL. It reads the absorbed-Q and sliced-K views
directly, converts BF16 to FP8, concatenates Q, and scatters KV in one launch.

## Diagnostic results

B300, TP8, full-architecture dummy Kimi K3, concurrency 1, MTP1 (verify M=2),
FP8 KV, greedy sampling; 10 s warmup + 20 s unprofiled measurement.

| Metric | Unfused target-verify baseline | Shared Triton + PDL |
|---|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 106.45 tok/s | 108.40 tok/s (+1.83%) |
| TPOT | 9.1597 ms | 8.9923 ms (-1.83%) |
| Rank-0 GPU target-verify median | 8.6397 ms | 8.4645 ms (-2.03%) |
| Preparation launches / MLA layer / verify step | 5 | 1 |

Across eight decode traces, the candidate executes 24 fused MLA preparations
per verification step: 288 launches over 12 steps per rank. This removes
96 launches per step/rank. Candidate per-rank kernel medians are 1.952–2.609 us,
measured from GPU profiler events, not host/event replay overhead.

These are short, non-interleaved dummy-model diagnostics; acceptance length
was 1.0 in both arms. They do not establish real-weight throughput, task quality,
or PDL's independent contribution.

Would sharing the existing decode preparation path with eligible target-verify
calls be an appropriate upstream change? The dispatch fix can be considered
separately from selecting CUDA versus Triton for the fused implementation.

_No response_

items.title: [Bug] Quantized DFlash2 draft silently yields ~0% acceptance — no error, no warning (the quiet counterpart to #36599)
items.body:
### Summary

A **quantized** DFlash2 draft checkpoint loads into `DFlash2DraftModel`, serves, and produces
drafts that are rejected ~100% of the time. There is **no error and no warning** — acceptance
simply collapses from ~3.7 to ~1.0 and decode drops below no-drafter speed.

The same weights **unquantized** work correctly. This is the silent counterpart to #36599 (quantized
NextN draft, `modelopt_fp4`), which fails loudly with a tensor-shape mismatch instead.

This is a read-only report — I have not root-caused it and am not opening a PR.

### Repro

Target: `Frozenlock/Qwen3.8-27B-int4-AutoRound` (auto-round, 4-bit, g128, sym).
Two drafters that are **the same model**, differing only in quantization:

| drafter | params | dtypes | quant |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` | 1,924,404,480 | BF16 | none |
| `syvai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W4A16` | 1,924,404,480 | I32 + BF16 | compressed-tensors |

Identical `architectures` (`DFlash2DraftModel`), identical `dflash_config`
(`block_size 8, selector_rank 256, selector_top_k 16`, same `target_layer_ids`), identical tensor
names including `candidate_selector.{hidden_projection.weight,predecessor_codebook,successor_codebook}`.

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <qwen3.8-27b-autoround-int4> \
  --tp-size 2 --quantization auto-round --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --context-length 262144 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 --max-running-requests 1 \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path <DRAFTER> \
  --speculative-draft-model-quantization <compressed-tensors | unquant>
```

### Result

| drafter | `accept len` | `accept rate` | decode (code) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| syvai (compressed-tensors) | **1.03** (n=422) | **0.004** | ~38 tok/s |
| z-lab (BF16, `unquant`) | **3.71** (n=100) | 0.61 | ~171 tok/s |

With the quantized drafter, `accept len` never exceeded **1.12** across 422 decode batches. At
`block_size 8` a working drafter reads 2–5. Decode is **slower than running with no drafter at
all**, because it pays full verify cost for zero accepted tokens.

### Why this is easy to miss

1. The draft loads into the correct class and logs success:
   `Load weight end. type=DFlash2DraftModel, quant=compressed-tensors`.
2. Speculative decoding **rejects** bad drafts, so correctness is preserved by construction — a
   0%-acceptance drafter is slow, never wrong. Output stays fluent and correct.
3. Our functional test suite reported **"All checks passed"** on the broken configuration
   (completion, tool calls, streaming, reasoning split, a 2K-token coherence check, vision).

The only signal is the engine's own `accept len:` / `accept rate:` counters in the decode-batch log.

### What I ruled out

- **Not an architecture-mapping failure.** `DFlash2DraftModel` is first-class
  (`srt/models/dflash.py:1066`) and listed in
  `model_executor/model_runner_components/spec_aux_hidden_state.py`.
- **Not the target's aux-hidden-state capture.** #38589 reports that gap for `Qwen4Exp` and
  explicitly names `qwen3_5.py` — our target — as the *working* parent.
- **Not tensor naming.** Byte-for-byte identical between the two checkpoints.
- **Not the target `lm_head`.** Ours is dense BF16, satisfying the DFlash2 selector's dense path.

### Leading hypothesis (untested)

The `CandidateSelector` codebooks / `hidden_projection` are loaded through the compressed-tensors
path and end up wrong — well-formed but not the trained values — so the selector emits confident
garbage. That would match the symptom exactly: loads clean, runs, drafts nothing acceptable.

### Suggested mitigation regardless of root cause

Warn (or refuse) when a DFLASH draft resolves to a quantized checkpoint, as #36599 suggests for the
NextN path. A one-line boot warning would have saved a full benchmark cycle here.

### Related

- #36599 — same class (draft quant config mishandled), NextN/`modelopt_fp4`, fails loudly.
- #38589 — DFlash aux-hidden-state capture on `Qwen4Exp`.
- #36118 — runs `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` successfully (accepted span 4.49 @10K), consistent with
  the BF16 arm here.

### Environment

- SGLang `v0.5.19` (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19`), stock, no patches
- 2× RTX 3090 (sm_86), PCIe, no NVLink, TP=2, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`
- Downstream context: https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090 (SGLang tier for Qwen3.8-27B)

⚠️ One SGLang-specific footgun found while narrowing this down, in case it is worth documenting
separately: `--speculative-draft-model-quantization` defaults to the **target's** quantization when
unset (`arg_groups/serving_hook.py:629`). Pointing at a BF16 drafter without passing `unquant`
therefore applies the target's `auto-round` to BF16 weights and reproduces the identical
0%-acceptance symptom from the other direction.

items.title: [Bug] FLUX.2 rejects --attention-backend sage_attn: model-level whitelist excludes SAGE_ATTN (regression since #22423)
items.body:
## Summary

On FLUX.2 (`black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv`), `--attention-backend sage_attn` fails at model construction:

```
ValueError: Attention backend 'sage_attn' is not supported by this attention layer;
supported backends: ['aiter', 'torch_sdpa', 'aiter_sage', 'fa'] for component 'transformer'
```

SageAttention is installed and its CUDA resolver is registered, so this is not a missing dependency — the FLUX.2 model class hard-codes a whitelist that excludes `SAGE_ATTN`.

## Root cause

`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py`, class `Flux2Transformer2DModel`:

```python
# FLUX.2 stays closer to the official diffusers output with Torch SDPA.
# The generic FA path still produces a measurable image-level drift here.
_supported_attention_backends = {
    AttentionBackendEnum.TORCH_SDPA,
    AttentionBackendEnum.FA,
    AttentionBackendEnum.AITER,
    AttentionBackendEnum.AITER_SAGE,
}
```

This set is passed to every `Flux2TransformerBlock` / `Flux2SingleTransformerBlock`.
`selector._is_backend_supported()` is strict membership, so `SAGE_ATTN` raises.

Introduced by #22423 ("[diffusion] fix: fix flux2 i2i accuracy", 2026-04-10). Before that commit FLUX.2 declared no whitelist, so `sage_attn` was selectable. `AITER`/`AITER_SAGE` were added later by #22802 for AMD ROCm; they are not usable on CUDA (`aiter_sage` → `Invalid attention backend for cuda`), so listing them does not restore a Sage path on NVIDIA.

Note the comment only justifies preferring Torch SDPA over the generic FA path; it does not explain why `SAGE_ATTN` is excluded.

## Reproduction

- GPU: RTX 5090 (sm_120, Blackwell, 32 GB)
- sglang: v0.5.19 dev build (`0.0.0.dev1+g95f5ecd3d`, release/v0.5.19); also reproduces on upstream `lmsysorg/sglang:latest`
- deps: `sageattention 2.2.0`, `torch 2.13.0+cu130`, `flash-attn-4 4.0.0b19`
- model: `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv`

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path /mnt/models/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv \
  --attention-backend sage_attn \
  --ulysses-degree=1 --ring-degree=1 \
  --num-gpus 1 --port 30000 --host 0.0.0.0
```

## Impact

- `sage_attn` is documented as a first-class diffusion backend and is the recommended fast path on Blackwell consumer GPUs (FA4 cannot run on sm_120). Users following the docs on a 5090 hit a hard failure with no documented workaround.
- Passing an unsupported backend silently degrades to the **diffusers native** implementation (`Error while loading customized transformer, falling back to native version`), which is worse than a clean error.
- There is no escape hatch: `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_BACKEND=sage_attn` and `--component-attention-backends transformer=sage_attn` both go through the same strict check and raise.
- The attention_backends docs page only lists backends/platforms and does not describe per-model whitelists, so the restriction is invisible from the docs.

## Related

- #34389 (closed) reported the same class of problem: #33707 changed the behavior from "requested backend not in a component's supported set → fall back to SDPA" to "raise an error". That issue is closed, but FLUX.2 + `sage_attn` still hard-fails, because the FLUX.2 DiT *explicitly declares* a set that excludes `SAGE_ATTN` rather than declaring nothing.

## Requested change

One of:

1. Add `AttentionBackendEnum.SAGE_ATTN` back to FLUX.2's `_supported_attention_backends` (opt-in), or
2. Provide an explicit override (env var / flag) that lets users force a backend even when a model declares a narrower set, or
3. If the exclusion is intentional for accuracy reasons, document per-model restrictions and make the error actionable (currently it fails at model construction with no hint that this is intentional).

## Verification that it used to work

Checked `flux_2.py` across upstream commits: no `_supported_attention_backends` at `2e053d6eb6` (2026-02-24), `da9dcbc906` (2026-03-04), `d633ab7349` (03-27), `68a4573627` (03-31), `2b119ba388` (04-05), `10b18b8b29` (04-05); first appears at `7c6b5c095c` = #22423 (2026-04-10). Whitelist unchanged at `d0035da34e` (2026-09-11).

items.title: [Bug] Kimi-K3: aborting a request mid-prefill kills every rank — `free_kv_row_segments` asserts "segment at N shares a page with the one ending at N"
items.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] The bug has not been fixed in the latest version (still present at `0fadad89`, 2026-09-11).
- [x] I have provided the exact traceback, launch arguments and image tags below.

### Describe the bug

On Kimi-K3 with the unified hybrid SWA cache, aborting a request while it is still being prefilled (client disconnect, or a proxy's time-to-first-byte deadline) makes **every scheduler rank** raise inside the KV free path and the server exits:

```
File "srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py", in process_batch_result_prefill
    release_kv_cache(req, self.tree_cache)
File "srt/mem_cache/common.py", in release_kv_cache
    tree_cache.cache_finished_req(
File "srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py", in cache_finished_req
    self.free_kv_row(req.kv, ranges)
File "srt/mem_cache/base_prefix_cache.py", in free_kv_row
    free_kv_row_segments(
File "srt/mem_cache/common.py", in free_kv_row_segments
    allocator.free_segments(swa_alive)
File "srt/mem_cache/allocator/base.py", in free_segments
    for free_index, start_pos in self._page_disjoint(segments):
File "srt/mem_cache/allocator/base.py", in _page_disjoint
    assert prev_end is None or start_pos // ps > (prev_end - 1) // ps, (
AssertionError: segment at 32704 shares a page with the one ending at 32704
```

Seen on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260906-09daea94` (three production crashes in two days: boundaries 50496, 85312, 77056) and on `nightly-dev-cu13-20260910-00840301` (boundary 32704, reproduced within 3 minutes of a replay of real traffic). #38159 is in the 09-10 image and does not touch this path (it rerouted `free_swa_out_of_window_slots`).

### Why it happens

`UnifiedRadixCache.cache_finished_req` frees a request whose `effective_cache_len < len(token_ids)` (i.e. truncated by an abort) as **two ranges that touch**:

```python
ranges = [(page_aligned_len, len(kv_indices))]          # kv_indices was cut to effective_cache_len
if tail_free_start is not None:
    ranges.append((tail_free_start, len(kv_indices_full)))  # tail_free_start == effective_cache_len
self.free_kv_row(req.kv, ranges)
```

`free_kv_row_segments` hands them to `allocator.free_segments` as separate segments, and `_page_disjoint` requires the second one to start on a fresh page. `effective_cache_len` is not page-aligned in general, so the shared boundary page trips the assert. The comment right above ("the tail free is deferred and batched with the unaligned tail below so a shared boundary page is emitted once") describes the intent; the batching never merges the two ranges.

Every instance was preceded within one second by an `/abort_request` for a request with a 120–200K-character prompt in chunked prefill (`#pending-token` ≈ 500K at the time).

### Reproduction

- Kimi-K3, `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-draft-model-path <DSpark> --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --linear-attn-decode-backend triton --linear-attn-verify-backend triton --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-running-requests 76 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --skip-server-warmup`, `page_size` auto-set to 64 (`CuteDSL MLA only supports page_size of 32 or 64`), 8×B300.
- Send a burst of long multimodal chat completions (100K+ characters, several images) to a cold server, and abort some of them (`/abort_request` or client disconnect) while they are still prefilling. All ranks die within minutes.

### Proposed fix

Coalesce touching segments of the one kv row in `free_kv_row_segments` before the SWA dead/alive split: slices of the same row that touch are exactly the slice they were cut from, so merging frees every page once and no boundary is checked twice. PR to follow. We have been running this as a build-time patch in production since 2026-09-11 01:47 UTC with the same trigger (TTFB-deadline aborts) survived.

### Environment

- Images: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260906-09daea94`, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260910-00840301`
- Hardware: 8× NVIDIA B300 (SM103), NCCL 2.30.7
- Model: Kimi-K3 + Kimi-K3-DSpark draft

items.body:
### Summary

`flash_attn_with_kvcache` is advertised as working on sm_89 and fails there with a raw CUDA error instead of a clean rejection. Two separate things combine to produce it, and I think the second one is a plain bug.

### Environment

- GPU: RTX 4080 SUPER, **sm_89** (Ada), driver via CUDA 13.0 container
- `sglang-kernel==0.4.5+cu130` (also verified against `0.4.6.post1`)
- torch 2.11.0+cu130, Python 3.12
- Called through a third-party engine, not SGLang itself, so this is about the kernel package's contract rather than a serving regression.

### What happens

```
CUDA error (_deps/repo-flash-attention-src/hopper/flash_fwd_launch_template.h:203): invalid argument
```

The model loads fully and the failure comes at the first kernel launch (CUDA-graph capture), so it is a launch-time gap and not a build or link problem.

### Why, with evidence

`is_fa3_supported()` accepts compute capability major 8, and the comment above it names this card:

```python
#  Right now, fa3 is supported for sm80/sm87 and sm86/sm89. ...
#  And for sgl-kernel right now, we can build fa3 on sm80/sm86/sm89/sm90a.
#  That means if you use A100/A*0/L20/L40/L40s/4090 you can use fa3.
return (torch.version.cuda >= "12.3") and (
    torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] == 9
    or torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] == 8
)
```

But the published wheels carry no sm_89 cubin for `flash_ops`:

```
cuobjdump --list-elf sgl_kernel/flash_ops.abi3.so | grep -oE 'sm_[0-9]+' | sort -u

  0.4.5+cu130     -> sm_80 sm_86 sm_90
  0.4.6.post1     -> sm_80 sm_86 sm_90
```

So `is_fa3_supported()` returns `True` on a card whose kernels were not built, and the FA3 launch resolves to the `hopper/` template with nothing to run.

The FA2 kernels for this architecture *are* present -- `flash_ops` exports `fa2`, `fa3` and `mha_fwd`, with 372 `sm_80` and 372 `sm_86` cubins -- but there is no way to reach them from this entry point. In `flash_attn.py` on current `main`, `ver` is a dead parameter: it appears only as the default `ver=3` in two signatures (lines 71 and 302) and is never read or forwarded. Both call sites go to the same `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fwd.default(...)`, so a caller passing `ver=2` gets FA3 regardless.

### Expected

Either of these would be an improvement, and they are independent:

1. `is_fa3_supported()` should agree with what the wheel actually contains, so an unsupported card raises the existing `NotImplementedError("flash_attn at sgl-kernel is only supported on sm90 and above")` instead of a CUDA error from inside a kernel launch. Right now that guard passes on sm_89 and the error surfaces much later and much less legibly.
2. Either honour `ver` and dispatch to the FA2 kernels already shipped for sm_80/sm_86, or drop the parameter so callers are not led to believe the choice exists. A downstream engine is currently computing a version and passing it in good faith.

If the intent is the docstring's claim, then adding sm_89 to the FA3 build arch list would be the third option, and the comment suggests it is expected to work.
